newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh c. bank reserves edge up to $1.31 bln Apr 1.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh c. bank reserves edge up to $1.31 bln Apr 1.

text.p: Kazakhstan's net reserves of hard currency and gold rose slightly to 98.35 billion tenge ($1.31 billion) on April 1 from 96.90 million on March 1, the National Bank said on Wednesday.
Net reserves on April 1 last year were $1.27 billion.
At the start of this year the Central Asian state's reserves were 101.9 billion tenge ($1.36 billion).

Lower gold prices on international markets and high demand for hard currency on the domestic market stood behind the 3.55 billion tenge decrease in Kazakhstan's reserves in the first quarter of this year, the National Bank said.

It said that hard-currency reserves fell in January-March by 2.04 billion tenge, while gold reserves fell by 1.53 billion tenge. The bank provided no absolute figures for Kazakhstan's gold and hard currency reserves.
